subject: URGENT: FastLedger performance degradation — request for burst & credit approval
messages:
From: Jill Ramos <jill@fastledger.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-15T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency — immediate help needed

Lauren —

We're seeing sustained latency spikes and intermittent 5xx errors against our /v1/generate endpoint since 07:45 PT. P50 has climbed from ~120ms to ~1.3s and we're seeing a 5xx rate around 1.8% over the last 30m. This is happening against our reserved capacity (FL-9374) — requests are failing even though our dashboard shows the reservation as active.

This is customer-visible: search/autocomplete flows are timing out. We have a large retention event tonight and this behavior here puts renewal at risk. Can you escalate?

I've attached a short screenshot of the latency spike and a token-rate dump.

Thanks,
Jill Ramos
Head of Platform, FastLedger

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-15T08:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors and latency — immediate help needed

Quick triage from infra: we're seeing sustained queue depth and token enqueue latency on the dedicated pool in us-west-2 that's serving FL-9374. Several adjacent reservations recently spiked (unknown noisy neighbor) and autoscaler didn't trigger because the pool is pinned to reserved capacity. Evidence: kernel-level queue metrics, KV-cache miss rate increased 4x.

Immediate mitigation options (short-lived):
- Route a % of FastLedger traffic to a hosted compatibility variant (same model family, quantized) — avoids token routing into the saturated pool but will increase per-token cost.
- Enable aggressive batching + prefix KV caching for FastLedger routes for the next 2 hours (low-risk, may reduce tail latency).
- Approve burst GPU quota (request +2 reserved GPUs for 4 hours) — requires exec approval for overage and a one-time credit negotiation.

I'll assemble a one-page tech summary and an ops playbook for the next 60 minutes. If Lauren can confirm willingness to route traffic briefly, we can start the switch and roll back once load normalizes.

— Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer (Serving Runtime)
[inline: metrics snippet attached to incident channel]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-15T09:03:00Z
Subject: Exec approval requested: +2 GPU burst for FastLedger (FL-9374) and one-time credit

David —
FastLedger is experiencing production degradations tied to dedicated pool saturation in us-west-2. Karthik's assessment suggests we can remediate within minutes by either routing a portion of traffic to hosted variants or provisioning +2 GPUs temporarily. The customer has a high-profile retention event tonight; we risk renewal if we don't act fast.

Proposed ask: approve a 4-hour +2 GPU burst allocation for the dedicated pool (cost to Redwood ~ $X/hr) and authorize a goodwill credit of one billing month if we require routing to hosted (to cover their increased token spend). We'll track and reconcile with finance.

I'll make the routing change immediately if you approve; we prefer to avoid a hard failover without notice.

Requesting a quick thumbs-up so we can proceed.

— Lauren

From: david_kim@redwood.ai

Lauren — approved.
- +2 GPUs for 4 hours (ops: allocate now and confirm when live).
- Pre-approve one-month goodwill credit for FastLedger if routing is necessary; finance to reconcile post-incident.

Please document the decision in the incident channel and copy me on the customer message. If we end up routing more than 24 hours, escalate for commercial review.

— David

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Jill Ramos <jill@fastledger.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <ops@fastledger.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-17T19:03:00Z
Subject: FastLedger incident update — temporary measures and next steps

Jill —
Following up with a concrete plan and what we executed:

What we saw: dedicated pool headroom in us-west-2 reached saturation causing elevated queueing and a 5xx rate ~1.8% (see attached snapshot).

What we did (timeline):
- 2027-05-15 09:20Z: Allocated +2 GPUs to the dedicated pool (4-hour burst).
- 2027-05-15 09:30Z: Enabled aggressive KV prefix caching and adjusted batching for your route — tail latency improved within 8 minutes.
- 2027-05-15 09:45Z: Began controlled routing of 25% traffic to a hosted, quantized-compatible variant to reduce pressure.

Customer-facing impact: These actions reduced the observed 5xx rate to <0.2% and p50 latency returned to ~140ms. No further user-visible issues reported during your retention event.

Commercial: David has pre-approved a one-month goodwill credit should routing to hosted be required; we'll have finance post the credit against FL-9374 once we finalize any reconciliation.

Next steps (owner):
- Karthik: deliver full incident RCA and proposed long-term guardrails (noisy neighbor protections, autoscale policy adjustments) by 2027-05-19 18:00Z.
- Marissa: propose a per-account fallback config we can ship as a checkbox in Console (target: 2027-05-31).
- Lauren: coordinate a short post-mortem with FastLedger this week; propose 30-min readout.

Attachments: latency_snapshot_20270515.png, SLA-excerpt-FastLedger.docx (highlighted).

We're sorry for the disruption — the team will run the RCA and bring recommended platform changes to prevent recurrence. Would 2027-05-18 14:00 PT for a 30-minute post-mortem work for you?

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
